Hazard Mitigation Funding Programs

BRIC: March 31, 2026 – Update: Please see the FY-2024/2025 Notice of Funding Opportunity for the Building Resilient Infrastructure Communities (BRIC) program.

FEMA Hazard Mitigation projects for Vermont towns and other eligible applicants for projects that reduce the risk of flooding or other hazards can include the following eligible project types:

  • Buyouts
  • Structural Elevations & Mitigation Reconstruction 
  • Natural resource projects such as floodplain restorations or dam removals
  • Infrastructure projects such as upsizing bridges or culverts
  • Floodproofing of municipal or commercial buildings
  • Road relocation, elevation, or soil stabilization

Application process:

  • Grants typically require a 25% local match. VEM can now cover 100% of local match for FY2023 Swift Current and Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) projects. Under HMGP, the following Disasters rounds are eligible for 100% local match: DR-4720, DR-4744, DR-4770, DR-4810, DR-4816, and DR-4826.

July 23, 2024: See the Amended Notice of Funding Opportunity for Vermont DR-4720 Hazard Mitigation Grant Program for more information, including changes to cost share, pre-application deadline, and pre-application submission requirements.

Hazard Mitigation Information & Support

Hazard Mitigation is sustained action taken to reduce or eliminate long-term risk to people and their property from hazards.

Hazard mitigation funds are available to municipalities and other organizations to help reduce or eliminate loss of life and property by taking measures to reduce the impacts of future disasters.

The Vermont Emergency Management Hazard Mitigation Team supports state agencies, non-profits, Regional Planning Commissions and municipalities in applying for and implementing projects under Hazard Mitigation grant programs.  We also support Regional Planning Commissions, municipalities, special districts, and other governmental entities in conducting natural hazard mitigation planning, and developing FEMA-approved Local Hazard Mitigation Plans.

2026 Hazard Mitigation Funding Opportunities

Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) Projects are currently being developed and implemented for DR-4720 (July 2023 flooding) and DR-4810 (July 2024 flooding). Funding is currently unavailable for new HMGP projects; however, entities interested in applying for future mitigation funding can submit projects such as property buyouts and elevations, floodproofing, floodplain restoration, and upsizing bridges and culverts to DPS.HazardMitigation@vermont.gov.

Flood Resilient Communities Fund (FRCF) was established by the Vermont Legislature under Act 74 with the intent of improving landscape and community resilience and reducing the future public safety and water quality impacts of flood hazards in Vermont, focusing on buyouts of flood-vulnerable properties. This program will prioritize projects that are not eligible for FEMA funding. Funding is currently unavailable, although towns and other eligible applicants are still encouraged to submit applications, which can be processed should more funding become available. 

Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) grant program for states and local communities to support mitigation activities. The funding available for FY2024/2025 is $2,000,000  federal share set-aside for Vermont. Funding can be used for project scoping, building code enhancements, and project implementation. Applications under BRIC are submitted through FEMA GO. State application deadline: May 15, 2026.   

Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA) grant program funds states, local communities, and other governmental entities to reduce or eliminate the risk of repetitive flood damage to buildings and structures insured under the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP). Funding can be used for project scoping, planning, individual structure flood mitigation, and localized flood risk reduction. The deadline to submit applications to the State in FEMA GO for FMA FY2024 was February 28, 2025.

Questions can be directed to: DPS.HazardMitigation@vermont.gov.
